t:
The power radiated from antenna of length l is proportional
to
s:
The power radiated by a linear antenna of length l transmitting electromagnetic waves of wavelength λ depends on its radiation resistance, R_rad. 

The radiation resistance of a dipole antenna is given by:
R_rad = 80π² (l/λ)²

Since the radiated power is P = I_rms² × R_rad (where I_rms is the antenna current), the power radiated is directly proportional to the radiation resistance:
P ∝ (l/λ)²

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

Options (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect because electromagnetic wave radiation theory shows that radiation resistance and radiated power vary strictly with the second power of the ratio of the antenna length to the wavelength, not linearly, cubically, or as a square root.
